required_assertion: For actual coprime odd fundamental discriminants D>1 and h*<0, F=Q(sqrt(Dh*)) and L=Q(sqrt D,sqrt h*) have disc(L)=(Dh*)² and L/F unramified. The restriction of chi_h* to G_F corresponds on Pic(O_F) to the quadratic norm character used in O.1. D=1 gives the trivial character.

derivations.name: Exact biquadratic discriminant by integral trace pairing
derivations.argument: Put alpha=(1+sqrt D)/2 and beta=(1+sqrt h*)/2. Cox5.13 supplies the two quadratic integer rings. A=Z[alpha,beta] has rank4 and is integral. For x in O_L, write x=a+b beta with a,b in Q(sqrt D). Both relative traces Tr(x) and Tr(beta*x) are integral in Q(sqrt D). The two-by-two trace matrix of1,beta has determinant h*, so solving this system shows h*a,h*b in Z[alpha], hence h*x in A. Interchanging the fields gives D*x in A. Since gcd(D,h*)=1, Bezout gives x in A, so A=O_L. The four embeddings show the trace matrix on1,alpha,beta,alpha*beta is the tensor product of the two quadratic trace matrices, up to basis ordering. Its determinant is D²(h*)², proving exactly the displayed equality. This is a local connecting derivation from the published quadratic integral bases, not a statement attributed verbatim to Cox.

derivations.name: Unramified genus extension
derivations.argument: The actual domain has F imaginary and d_F=D h* odd fundamental. Apply corrected Lemma6.8 with a=D: D divides d_F and D=1mod4. Thus F(sqrt D)=L is unramified, equivalently its relative discriminant ideal is1. This also follows from Theorem6.1 since D is a product of its signed prime discriminants. This direct published implication supplies the consumed unramified conclusion without assuming the discriminant equality as its own premise.

derivations.name: Actual norm character
derivations.argument: Write h* as the product of signed prime discriminants p*. Cox6.12–6.14 identifies the Artin action on each sqrt(p*) at any ideal a prime to2D h* by (Norm(a)/p). Quadratic reciprocity gives (p*/Norm(a))=(Norm(a)/p); multiplying over p|h* gives chi_h*(Norm(a)). This is exactly the restriction character on sqrt(h*), so it factors through Pic(O_F). Multiplicativity extends from prime ideals. Each ideal class admits an integral representative prime to2D h*: choose an element in the inverse ideal with the required minimal valuations at the finitely many excluded primes by the Chinese remainder theorem, and multiply the ideal by it. Thus choosing representatives prime to2D h* is an allowed strengthening of the manuscript choice prime to h*. This proves independence from the representative, not merely a formula on selected prime ideals. For the full finite-idelic equality, apply the independently accepted generic local norm/reciprocity theorem at each completion F_v/Q_p, and multiply over v|p. This identifies chi_h*(Norm a) with the restriction of chi_h* to G_F, so its local-unit factors are trivial because L/F is unramified. At the complex place the norm is positive, so the real sign character is trivial. This justifies the whole idelic expression, not only its value on convenient ideal representatives. The beta-specific conductor/unit bounds from that source are not used.

derivations.name: Exceptional case and conventions
derivations.argument: If D=1 then F=Q(sqrt h*) already contains sqrt h*, so the restricted character and the genus extension are trivial. No degree4 basis computation is applied in this case. Reversing arithmetic/geometric Artin conventions inverts a quadratic character and hence leaves its values unchanged.

retained_inputs: D and h* are the actual coprime odd fundamental discriminants from the fixed prepared domain, not arbitrary squarefree integers
Algebraic integers are closed under relative trace; elementary trace determinant and Bezout calculations
Usual ideal-class interpretation and arithmetic Artin convention, already supplied by accepted Cox class-field source
Chinese remainder theorem for ideals used only to choose a representative away from a finite set
excluded_claims: No new general local norm/reciprocity theorem
No new assertion about CM reduction, level orientations, genus-point nonvanishing or the subsequent theta comparison
No modification to original source freeze or canonical manuscript

additional_generic_input.scope: Generic finite-local-extension norm/reciprocity theorem before its beta-specific final application; nonnormal extensions allowed.
